chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the ivory, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it, and indeed I have a comb from it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is ivory considered halal or permissible for use in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Abdullah ibn Sulayman inquires about the permissibility of ivory, and Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms its validity by citing his personal possession of an ivory comb as practical evidence. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly principle of using the Imams' personal usage (*'urf* and *sunnah*) to validate the permissibility of materials not explicitly prohibited in the Quran, reinforcing the acceptability of luxury items for daily use.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the ivory, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it, and there is a comb for me<sup>asws</sup>, from it (ivory)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sulayman who has said the following: “
I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about ivory. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful and I have one ivory comb.’”
